title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Our repo has grown a number of slightly different CI workflows across packages and teams which increases maintenance burden and causes inconsistent caching and matrix behavior. This PR consolidates lint/test/release workflows into a shared, template-driven set of GitHub Actions, standardizes on Node 20 for JS/TS pipelines, and optimizes cache keys and parallelism to reduce CI runtime and improve cache hit rates. The changes target: 1) .github/workflows/*.yml consolidation into three canonical workflows (lint, test, release), 2) a new workflows/templates/ directory with reusable job definitions, 3) improved actions versions (bumped to recommended stable releases), 4) cache key hygiene to avoid thrashing between matrix axes, and 5) reduced duplicate jobs across top-level packages. Checklist: [x] Add templates and migrate existing workflows [x] Bump actions/checkout, setup-node, cache actions to supported versions [x] Standardize Node 20 build matrix where applicable [x] Improve cache key to include package-lock/hash + matrix dimension where necessary [x] Run full repo CI and patch flaky tests observed during initial run Notes on testing: Ran full CI in feature branch; initial test matrix had two flaky JS unit tests (infra/agent-client) which caused a rerun. After fixing a test fixture timing issue those jobs passed. Impact and migration notes: Teams that previously had bespoke additional jobs should import templates if they need custom steps; the shared templates are additive and maintain backward compatibility. Linked work items: ENG-3421 (CI consolidation initiative), ENG-3499 (cache parallelism improvements).

merge_details: Merged by Carlos Rivera via squash on main. Squash commit message: 'chore(ci): unify workflows and optimize cache parallelism (#781234)'. Merge strategy: squash and merge. CI green at merge time.
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows into template-driven lint/test/release pipelines, standardized Node 20 for JS workflows, bumped key GitHub Actions versions, and improved cache keying and parallelism. Result: ~25-35% faster CI runs for common PRs and fewer cache misses. No functional code changes for runtime behavior; some test flakes fixed.
